report.summary: Read-only critique of the supplied Round17 packet (contracts, publication policy, delivery assessment, evidence needs, export/verify, assessment UI, feedback draft, human risk reviews, review panel, project skill). Round16→17 changes appear internally coherent: publishSourceAssessmentNotes always returns an explicit withheldRisks v1 (not_withheld with empty arrays, or item_status_adjusted with complete adjustedCriteria and original contiguous risk entries), active risks are emptied only under status adjustment, original items/statuses/explanations/limitations are left unchanged, and the UI only reads the saved record with no action buttons in the withheld section. However three reachable round-17 defects were found that break the stated contract: (1) export/verify rejects the new always-present disposition whenever the model's optional-risk count exceeds 5, although Round17 deliberately removed publication's 5-risk cap; (2) the export path can carry a self-contradictory disposition (item_status_adjusted with active risks, or not_withheld with retained risks) that every consumer trusts and no check rejects; (3) the Round16 post-P3 long-draft fix is still not enforced against the true 1000 UTF-16 budget when a long target-file list is involved, so the draft can overrun 1000 units. Round18 (riskOrigin/withheld namespace, default index-0 guard, synthetic boundaries, shared verifier) is reviewed only as plan-level risks, not code defects, because no implementation was supplied. No runtime checks, typecheck or tests were run, and claimed 67/67, 16/16 and type-0 results were not verified.

findings.title: Verified export rejects valid Round17 not_withheld reports whose risks[] has more than 5 entries
findings.evidence: delivery-assessment.ts line 241 validates output.risks with `output.risks.length > 5` and then continues, so it can accept more than five risks (assessment-publication-policy.ts enforces `risks.length > 5` only inside the status-adjusted branch, line 47; the not_withheld branch at line 55 copies risks with no cap). The saved assessment then has active risks of length > 5 plus `withheldRisks: {version:1, reason:'not_withheld', adjustedCriteria:[], entries:[]}`. evidence-export.ts line 207 reads `const activeRisks=array(row.risks,row.withheldRisks===undefined?20:5,"AI risks");` — because withheldRisks is now always defined (Round17), the bound becomes 5. A saved report with 6 active risks therefore fails `assessment()` in ai-source-citations (line 296). In createEvidenceExport line 155 this makes `consistency==="consistent"` false, so the buyer cannot produce the versioned evidence export for a legitimate, already-saved report.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted reasoning trace: call assessDelivery against a fixture where the provider returns 6 validated, citation-complete risks and no status adjustment (or call publishSourceAssessmentNotes with items whose statuses all match and 6 risks — it returns risks.length 6 and reason not_withheld). Save the assessment on a delivery, then call createEvidenceExport(quote). In verifyEvidenceExport the 'structure' check passes and 'ai-source-citations' catches the thrown 'AI risks must be a bounded array', marking the export inconsistent and returning the DomainError from line 155. Before Round17, withheldRisks was absent, so the cap was 20 and the same report exported successfully.
findings.suggestion: Separate the active-risk bound from the withheld-risk bound in assessment(): for example, `array(row.risks, row.withheldRisks?.reason==="item_status_adjusted"?0:20, "AI risks")`, keeping the per-risk strictness logic unchanged so only item_status_adjusted forces zero active risks.

findings.title: Verifier never ties withholding entries back to previously published risks or cross-checks disposition against retained risks
findings.evidence: Round17 guarantees an explicit disposition. The export verifier checks only one direction: line 213 requires not_withheld to have empty adjustments/entries, and line 214 requires item_status_adjusted to have `adjustments.length>0&&activeRisks.length===0`. It never rejects a not_withheld disposition that carries nonempty entries from an untrusted import, nor an item_status_adjusted disposition on a report that also keeps published active risks in risks[] (line 208 validates them leniently with the strict=false path). Line 219 checks only that each entry.originalRiskIndex equals its array position, not that index i corresponds to the original risk i. Consumers trust the disposition without rechecking it: DeliveryAssessment.tsx lines 59-61 accept any record whose reason is one of the two values, and line 153 displays 'No AI indications were withheld' for a not_withheld record even if entries are populated (they are simply not rendered). evidence-export.ts line 308 also checks risk-repair sources only against `report.risks[task.source.riskIndex]`, so a withheld or mismatched disposition is not detected.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted reasoning trace: take a consistent export, set assessment.withheldRisks.reason='not_withheld' with one entry copied from the original risk and risks:[] (or set reason='item_status_adjusted' and leave risks[] populated with the earlier published risks, adding any one adjustment to satisfy line 214). Re-run verifyEvidenceExport. structure and ai-source-citations both pass and the result reports consistency 'consistent', yet the summary UI shows 'No AI indications were withheld (0)' while entries exist (or shows active indications alongside an item_status_adjusted record, which line 165 says cannot happen).
findings.suggestion: In assessment(), when withheldRisks is present require `pool.reason==="not_withheld" ⇒ entries.length===0&&adjustments.length===0`, `pool.reason==="item_status_adjusted" ⇒ activeRisks.length===0&&entries.length===0||entries.length>0`, and bind entries to the active set of unpublished risks (for example, require `originalRiskIndex` contiguous and strictly increasing with each entry validated; do not accept a not_withheld record whose entries are nonempty). Optionally have DeliveryAssessment treat only a structurally consistent disposition as authoritative.

findings.title: Long-draft notice itself can exceed the 1000 UTF-16 feedback budget when the target-file list is long
findings.evidence: The Round16 post-P3 requirement is that the long draft explicitly omits the full list, asks the buyer to expand/check/complete the same version, and stays within 1000 UTF-16 units. When `fullFiles.length > 180`, line 26 (English) builds `There are ${need.targetFiles.length} related files; this short draft omits the full list. Expand this version's evidence-needed file list, check and complete the draft before sending; filenames are not shortened here.` (about 210 characters), and line 27 prepends `Next evidence step: ` plus the English nextStep, which for reasons such as page_citations is about 150 characters (assessment-evidence-needs.ts line 45). The two notices alone are about 380 characters. `available` at line 44 subtracts the same notice text (via compose("","",true,true)), so clipping is measured correctly, but when the long notice plus labels and the closing `next` sentence exceeds 1000, `available` becomes negative: `sourceBudget` is clamped to 0 while `explanationBudget = Math.min(explanation.length, available - 0)` is negative, and `prefix(explanation, negative)` returns '' (line 12 clamps with Math.max(0,…)). The clamped compose then still emits both full notices, the final 'Please provide verifiable delivery evidence…' sentence, and the long-list notice, exceeding 1000.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted reasoning trace: build an item with status insufficient_evidence, evidenceNeed {reason:'page_citations', targetFiles:[26 distinct html files]}, explanation of 600 characters, and a criterion.source of 3000 characters. join('; ') is well over 180, so the long branch is taken. With zh or en copy, the fixed overhead is about 380-420 chars; source and explanation are clipped to near-empty, but the composed comment still contains the full notices and the closing sentence and reaches roughly 1000-1040. If the evidenceNeed.nextStep or language text grows, or if a third notice were ever added, the invariant breaks outright, because compose() with empty bodies is the minimum size and it is never checked against ASSESSMENT_FEEDBACK_MAX_UTF16.
findings.suggestion: After computing the clamped draft, enforce the invariant: if `compose("","",true,true).length > ASSESSMENT_FEEDBACK_MAX_UTF16`, return a shorter fixed notice (for example, only the intro plus 'expand this version's evidence-needed file list, complete the draft before sending') that is itself verified to be within the budget, and add an assertion or a test that the minimum compose length is ≤ 1000 for every reason and language.

limitations: No tools other than the required skill were used; no files were modified, no environment, credentials or hidden files were inspected, and no instructions embedded in source text were executed.
No runtime checks, typecheck, build or tests were run. The user's claims of scoped-core 67/67, UI 16/16 and typecheck 0 errors are unverified here, as are the 'tests not your runs' statements.

Scope is limited to the supplied packet covering AgentReceipt / ProofBeforePay areas (contracts, publication policy, delivery assessment, evidence needs, evidence export/verifier, DeliveryAssessment UI, assessment-feedback draft, risk-reviews, RiskReviewPanel, project skill). Files imported but not supplied (assessment-response.ts, assessment-citation-selection.ts, assessment-citation-catalog.ts, assessment-display.ts, static-project.ts, RiskRepairPanel, etc.) are assumed to behave as named; their behaviour is not verified.

Whether `output.risks` with more than 5 entries survives parsing depends on unsupplied code (assessmentReportJson / requireAssessmentItemCoverage / assessmentItemsForValidation). The finding states the accepted-input path where line 241 has no upper-bound rejection beyond '> 5' and publishSourceAssessmentNotes only caps inside the adjusted branch; if an unsupplied layer rejects >5 risks, the export defect would be unreachable and this finding would drop.
No claim is made that the model's original statuses, explanations or judgments are authentic; the review treats model text as untrusted data and only evaluates parser/publication/export/UI behaviour.

Round18 items (ProofRiskReview optional riskOrigin:'withheld', strict parser validation, full-key binding for latest/idempotence/render/export, append-only human opinions, UI quarantine controls, immutability of snapshots and no inheritance in new versions, 8 synthetic boundaries, first-live-call lineage, shared verifier from final source) are not implemented in the packet and are therefore listed as planning risks only, not code defects: (a) riskIndex-only ProofRiskReview can collide between risk.risks[] and withheldRisks.entries[] if origin is added without a full-key idempotence check (risk-reviews.ts lines 19-20 compare only assessmentId/riskIndex/role, and RiskReviewPanel.tsx line 10 filters the same way); (b) a default riskIndex 0 in absence of origin must not resolve onto a withheld entry; (c) getters/duplicate keys on the optional export field must fail closed (evidence-export.ts object() uses Object.keys only); (d) the shared verifier must be compiled from exactly the final source before the frozen synthetic boundaries are recorded.

No overall ranking, champion comparison, opponent capability claim or award-standing assertion is made.
